description: Words that matter in the campaign but aren't places on the map. category groups them on the Glossary page (in the order they first appear here). aliases: other spellings to find and link in the session notes (matched case-sensitively, so add lowercase forms too). see: related glossary ids, people ids or place ids. text: blank lines split paragraphs. Write only what the session notes say.

entries.name: Freya
entries.text: Goddess of nature, and one of the trinity. Her work is what people see most, so she is the one prayed to most. The commune and the Emerald Citadel are devoted to her: her holy symbol is on people and buildings all over the city, and a tree of life is set into the floor of the grand temple's sanctum in her honour.

entries.name: Lunareti
entries.text: God of night and the sea, and one of the trinity.

entries.name: Celestia
entries.text: The sun goddess, and one of the trinity.

entries.name: The trinity
entries.text:
The three deities the commune follows: Lunareti, Celestia and Freya. On this continent there are no divisions based on religion; conflict follows geography instead.

The cult of Xezus says the whole trinity is false, and that there are no gods.

entries.name: Xezus
entries.text:
Worshipped by the gnolls of the cave and by Valron's cult. The masked man found the gnolls in their cave and taught them about Xezus and their own power, and they bore its sign, the horned skull. The high priests of the Emerald Citadel were taken aback to hear of another deity.

According to Dion, Xezus is not a god at all: he is a massive, unknown creature as old as the dragons, not in any traditional teaching. A foundation-shaking entity of fire and earth from the era of dragons, who can share endless wisdom from his time here. Every member of the cult has met him.

Past the Northern Outpost, a secret path leads north through the forest and into the mountains to reach him.

entries.name: The cult of Xezus
entries.text:
Valron's followers, who travelled south with Dion in the black-robed caravan: pale, in black robes, hardened from living in the mountains. They don't seem crazy; they have all met Xezus, and are clear-headed in their beliefs.

They say the whole trinity is false and there are no gods: people were lied to, and the trinity keeps them weak and trapped. The three churches are wrong, and exiling people is a terrible crime. The dragons and the seals are real, but anybody can use magic, and with training people other than the Meruions could perform the seal. The Meruions could make a new seal with power from within, without relying on magic from the deities.

They want to spread the word by gathering the Meruions and opening their eyes to the truth of the world.

entries.name: The horned skull
entries.text: The sign of Xezus, borne by the gnolls of the cave. "It's our symbol," the last gnoll said, and it seems to include the masked man, whose mask has a white skull on it and whose gnolls bore the same brand.

entries.name: The Meruion
entries.text:
A god's champion. Dion is Freya's next Meruion: he will ascend when he is 19. The current Meruion, a very old half-elf, sits on a throne in the grand temple giving blessings, and is meant to pass his power on to Dion.

The Meruions must go to the Scorched Lands to renew the seal on the chromatic dragons. Dion is being raised and taught to go with the other two Meruions, and because the current one is so old, he is badly needed back.

The cult of Xezus wants to gather the Meruions and open their eyes; Dion now says the Meruions should be collected and the ritual stopped. The cult believes the Meruions could make a new seal with their own power, without the deities' magic.

The commune is life-bound to the Meruion until he reaches ascendancy.

entries.name: The original Meruions
entries.text: The first champions. When the metallic dragons were losing to the chromatic dragons, the gods raised a champion in each realm. The champions took the chromatic dragons to the Scorched Lands and sealed them in the abyss, the bottomless chasm in front of the Tree of Life, using so much magic that they crystallised.

entries.name: The crystal woman
entries.text: A glowing green crystalline female figure, suspended in the air beyond the Meruion's throne in the grand temple's sanctum.

entries.name: Archdruid
entries.text: The commune's leader, who kept it safe: totems around the clearing made anyone approaching see an illusion of a rock face and go around. The archdruid was Allister, Dion's teacher.

entries.name: The high priests
entries.text: The leaders of the grand temple of Freya in the Emerald Citadel. They are all elven, as are most of the priests and leaders. They sent seasoned scouts to search the northern mountains, and gave the party work in the city in the meantime.

entries.name: Magic colours
entries.text: Until now, the party has only seen magic cast in the colour of its goddess: Freya's magic is green and silver. Among the cult, Dion has seen magic of many colours, and now casts through himself: his Goodberry glows a beautiful red, his favourite colour.

entries.name: Sentients
entries.text: What the books call every creature. The elves were the first; the dragonborn are the youngest.

entries.name: Dragonborn
entries.text:
The youngest of the Sentients. What racism exists in this world is mostly aimed at dragonborn, because of the history of the evil chromatic dragons.

The Draconic language is hardly spoken, and is taboo.

entries.name: Chromatic dragons
entries.text:
The first creatures to spring from the Tree of Life. They were destructive, and were going to annihilate the world. They burned the tree to a crisp and destroyed it to stop it making more life, which made the Scorched Lands; no new life has come from the tree in thousands of years. The original Meruions sealed them in the abyss, a massive bottomless chasm in front of the tree.

Because of them, what racism exists is mostly aimed at dragonborn, and Draconic is hardly spoken and taboo.

entries.name: Metallic dragons
entries.text: The last thing the Tree of Life made, to fight the chromatic dragons. They were still losing when the gods raised the original Meruions.

entries.name: Giants
entries.text: One of the species the Tree of Life made to slow the chromatic dragons. They are believed gone, after losing a war against the dragons.

entries.name: Renown
entries.text:
The party's standing with its faction, which grew over three years in the Emerald Citadel.

1: Poor. 2: Rent an apartment. 3: Buy an apartment. 4: Buy a home.

entries.name: Moonsugar
entries.text: A drug. Clover became addicted to it during the three years in the Emerald Citadel.

entries.name: A Unique Perspective on Things That Already Happened
entries.text: Golgamutt's massive best seller, written while he was a researcher at the grand library. It paid for his house in The Heights. Roslow and Jimothy both own copies, and asked him to sign them.
